subject: Energy
title: The Hydrogen Hype Check
description: Learn The Hydrogen Hype Check in one minute.

hook.text: Hydrogen is often overhyped—promoted for uses where batteries or direct electrification would be far more efficient.

buildup.text: Hydrogen cars lose 3x more energy than EVs—electrolysis, compression, and fuel cells waste most of the input power.

discovery.text: Hydrogen makes sense only where direct electricity can't work—heavy industry, shipping, aviation, and seasonal storage.

twist.text: Fossil fuel companies promote hydrogen for home heating—but heat pumps are 3–5 times more efficient for that job.

climax.text: The risk is using hydrogen to delay electrification—keeping gas infrastructure alive when better solutions exist.

punchline.text: Right fuel, right job—hydrogen isn't for everything.

quiz.question: Why are hydrogen cars less efficient than EVs?
options: Energy is lost in electrolysis, compression, and conversion
